subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Road rage: Listening 4.3.2, advice and role play
outcomes: Understand what road rage is and what makes drivers angry
Give advice to drivers to help them stay calm
Role-play a polite dialogue between two drivers

tf.s: Road rage is violent or aggressive behaviour by drivers.
tf.why: Yes, road rage means drivers acting angrily and aggressively.

tf.s: Tailgating means driving too close to the car in front.
tf.why: Correct, tailgating is following too closely.

tf.s: The driver who is tailgated feels relaxed and safe.
tf.why: Tailgating makes drivers feel nervous because it is dangerous.

tf.s: Flashing your lights at other drivers is seen as rude and aggressive.
tf.why: Right, it tries to push other drivers out of the way.

tf.s: Not using indicators is confusing for other drivers.
tf.why: Yes, they don't know if you will go left or right.

tf.s: When someone cuts in, the other driver may have to brake sharply.
tf.why: Correct, cutting in can force a sudden stop.

tf.s: Good advice for an angry driver is to drive faster than the other car.
tf.why: The advice is to stay calm and let the other driver pass.
Yes, keeping cool means not getting angry.

tf.s: Indicators are used to light the road at night.
tf.why: Indicators show other drivers which way you are turning.

tf.s: 'Cutting in' means driving slowly at the back of a long line of cars.
tf.why: Cutting in means moving suddenly in front of another car.

boxes.why: Road rage is angry, aggressive driving.

o: driving too close behind a car
boxes.why: Tailgating means following another car too closely.

boxes.q: How does not signalling make other drivers feel?
boxes.why: They don't know which way the driver will turn.

boxes.q: How are flashing lights described in the listening?
boxes.why: Flashing lights try to push drivers out of the way.

boxes.q: What must a driver do when someone cuts in?
boxes.why: Cutting in forces the driver to stop suddenly.

boxes.q: Which is good advice for an angry driver?
boxes.why: Staying calm helps avoid road rage.

o: which way a car will turn
boxes.why: Indicators signal a turn left or right.

boxes.q: Which is a polite thing to say to another driver?
o: Sorry, I didn't see you - go ahead.
boxes.why: Polite words help calm both drivers.

boxes.q: What does 'let the other driver pass' mean?
o: allow them to go in front
boxes.why: Letting them pass ends the problem calmly.

hunt.q: Lights that show you will turn
Moving suddenly in front of a car

mcq.q: Which behaviour is an example of road rage?
o: shouting and flashing lights at drivers
waiting calmly at a red light
mcq.why: Road rage is angry and aggressive behaviour.

o: the car behind may not be able to stop in time
mcq.why: Being too close leaves no time to stop.

mcq.q: Why are unsignalled turns a problem?
o: drivers don't know if the car will go left or right
mcq.why: Without signals, other drivers must guess.

mcq.q: Which phrase means the same as 'stay calm'?
mcq.why: Keep cool means don't get angry.

mcq.q: A car is driving very close behind you. What is the best thing to do?
o: stay calm and let it pass
mcq.why: Letting it pass is the safest choice.

mcq.q: You turn without using your indicator and another driver is angry. What could you say?
mcq.why: An apology helps calm the other driver.

mcq.q: A driver suddenly moves in front of you. What is this called?
mcq.why: Cutting in is moving suddenly in front of another car.

mcq.q: Why is flashing lights at other drivers described as rude?
o: it tries to push other drivers out of the way
it helps them see the road
it is a way to say thank you
mcq.why: It is aggressive pressure on other drivers.

mcq.q: Why is giving calm advice better than getting angry?
mcq.why: Angry drivers take risks that cause accidents.

mcq.q: What do all four drivers in the listening have in common?
mcq.why: Each one talked about something another driver did.
